figure: # docs/deliverable/FIGURES.tsv — P13f. figure <TAB> script <TAB> source.
# EVERY figure in the deliverable is produced by a COMMITTED script from COMMITTED
# numbers, and is listed here. No model-generated imagery, no hand-drawn imagery: a
# chart in an economics paper has to BE the data. This is P6's rule pointed at the
# pictures.
# THE CORPUS HAS ZERO FIGURES TODAY. Measured, not assumed, over the four manuscripts
# named by PAPERS= in build.sh: eight reference patterns find nothing, no image file is
# tracked anywhere in the repository, the built 145-page PDF carries zero image
# XObjects, and preamble.tex does not even load graphicx — the deliverable currently
# cannot render a figure at all.
# So this file has no figure rows, and an empty file is exactly the trap: it would close
# P13f VACUOUSLY and reopen it in SILENCE the day someone pastes in the first chart. The
# @zero-figures row below is therefore not a figure — it is a CLAIM, and the claim is
# under guard:
#   scripts/wt177_figure_guard.py   refuses @zero-figures the moment a manuscript
#                                   references a figure (SENTINEL-WITH-FIGURES), refuses
#                                   its removal while the count is still zero
#                                   (SENTINEL-MISSING), refuses an unlisted figure
#                                   (UNLISTED-FIGURE), a row whose script or source does
#                                   not exist (ROW-SCRIPT-MISSING / ROW-SOURCE-MISSING),
#                                   and a row nothing uses (ORPHAN-ROW).
#   tests/test_figures_manifest_bites.py   binds all of that to the suite, so it runs
#                                   without anyone remembering to run it.
# WHEN THE FIRST FIGURE LANDS: add its row, DELETE the @zero-figures row, and re-emit the
# receipt with `python3 scripts/wt177_figure_guard.py --emit`. The guard will not let you
# do three of those four and call it done.
# FORMAT: three tab-separated fields. No blank lines — the P13f criterion's awk runs
# `test -f ""` on one and fails with nothing to explain why; the guard refuses it first.
@zero-figures
